item.title: District of Columbia Charter Schools: Key Changes Made to Academic Accountability System
item.description:
What GAO Found
The DC Public Charter School Board (PCSB) uses a multi-step process, including interviews and public hearings, to screen applicants. PCSB also requires applicants to meet several decision criteria (see figure). In the past 5 years PCSB has made a few key changes to the charter school application process. Changes include requiring that charters fill a demonstrated need and that prospective schools complete a preapplication process. Additionally, PCSB has shifted the application timeline to the fall from the spring.
DC Public Charter School Board (PCSB) Application Decision Criteria
Note: For more details, see figure 1 in GAO-27-109048
In the last 5 years, two schools applied for new charters and PCSB denied both. By comparison, in the previous 5 years (2016–2021), PCSB received 30 applications and approved 11. PCSB officials attributed the reduced number of applications to the more rigorous application process. For the 2026 application cycle, PCSB did not receive any applications.
PCSB uses several mechanisms to monitor charter schools’ academic performance and compliance with applicable legal requirements. In 2024 PCSB introduced the Annual School Performance Index Report and Evaluation (ASPIRE) system, which is intended to improve accountability for schools’ success and student development. PCSB also uses ASPIRE to determine which schools need additional monitoring or support. While the ASPIRE system has similar measures to PCSB’s previous system, ASPIRE emphasizes school performance. ASPIRE calculates performance measures by student groups, such as students with disabilities or multilingual learners, rather than for all students combined.
Why GAO Did This Study
Almost one-half of DC’s public-school students were enrolled in 133 charter schools during school year 2025–26. The District of Columbia, School Reform Act of 1995, as amended, requires PCSB—DC’s sole chartering authority—to review and approve charter applications, monitor schools, and submit annual reports on its work.
The District of Columbia Appropriations Act of 2005, as amended, included a provision for GAO to review DC’s chartering authorities every 5 years. This report describes changes in the 5 years since our last report (2016–2021) in how PCSB reviews applications, monitors charter schools and takes corrective actions, and how PCSB complies with its annual reporting requirements, among other objectives.
GAO reviewed PCSB policies and procedures, including the 2026 Charter Application Guidelines, Charter Review and Charter Renewal guidelines, and policy documents related to PCSB’s new accountability system. GAO also compared PCSB’s 2026 Annual Report to School Reform Act requirements and interviewed PCSB’s board chair and staff.
For more information, contact Jacqueline M. Nowicki at NowickiJ@gao.gov.
